name: Eternal Ltd
about: Incorporated in 2010, Eternal Limited (previously Zomato Limited) is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Eternal has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers. [1]

sections.one_liner: Indian food delivery and quick-commerce platform. The question now: can a 3.1% EBITDA margin grow while capex burns cash?
business: Quick commerce was 69.5% of FY26 revenue and grew 626%. It now buys and sells its own stock, so it books the full value of goods. [AR FY26]
Rest of FY26 revenue: food delivery 18.7% (+26%), B2B supplies 9.9% (-13%), going-out 1.8% (+32%). [AR FY26]
India only, mostly top metros. Dark-store mix is moving from 80% urban / 20% tier-2/3 toward smaller cities. [AR FY26] [Q4FY26 call]
The inventory switch inflates reported revenue. Sep-25 quarter revenue jumped 89.6% QoQ, so growth before and after cannot be compared. [Numbers]
financial_snapshot: Q2FY27: revenue Rs 24,138 cr (+77.6% YoY), EBITDA Rs 752 cr (3.1% margin), PAT Rs 125 cr (0.5% margin). [Numbers]
TTM: revenue Rs 77,956 cr, EBITDA Rs 2,200 cr (2.8%), PAT Rs 493 cr. Only 22% of EBITDA reaches PAT. [Numbers]
ROCE 2.48%, ROE 0.38%. TTM PAT of Rs 493 cr on Rs 31,275 cr net worth is a 1.6% return. [Numbers]
Market cap Rs 3,31,634 cr: 673x P/E, about 4.3x TTM sales, about 151x TTM EBITDA, 10.6x book. Price Rs 344 vs 52-week high Rs 346. [Numbers]
trajectory: 5-year revenue CAGR 93.7%, to Rs 54,364 cr in FY26. Most of FY26's +169% comes from booking goods at full value. [Numbers] [AR FY26]
EBITDA went from Rs -1,851 cr (FY22) to Rs 1,208 cr (FY26). Quarterly EBITDA rose six quarters in a row, Rs 115 cr to Rs 752 cr. [Numbers]
FY26 PAT fell 31% to Rs 366 cr while EBITDA rose 90%. Costs below EBITDA ate the gain; breakdown not disclosed. [Numbers]
Sep-26 margin of 3.1% equals FY25's, but on a larger gross revenue base. That implies real unit-margin gains. YoY growth slowed 182% to 77.6% as the base caught up. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings rose 7.7x, from Rs 749 cr (Mar-24) to Rs 5,757 cr (Sep-26). D/E went from 0.04 to 0.18. [Numbers]
Cash conversion cycle went from -54 days (FY25) to +2 days (FY26). Inventory days rose 12 to 26, so free supplier funding is gone. [Numbers]
Since Mar-25, net worth rose only Rs 958 cr while borrowings rose Rs 3,712 cr. Growth is now debt-funded; cash balance not disclosed. [Numbers]
cash_quality: 3-year CFO/PAT is 1.27x. FY26 was 1.73x (CFO Rs 632 cr vs PAT Rs 366 cr), but FY25 was only 0.58x. [Numbers]
FCF fell from Rs 444 cr (FY24) to Rs -623 cr (FY25) and Rs -1,114 cr (FY26). Implied capex rose from Rs 202 cr to Rs 1,746 cr. [Numbers]
FY24-26 cumulative FCF was Rs -1,293 cr while borrowings rose Rs 3,843 cr. Reported profits are not yet paying for growth. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Annual report claims 'disciplined cost efficiency', yet FY26 PAT fell 31%, FCF was Rs -1,114 cr and borrowings more than doubled. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
The Q1 claim that competition peaked fits Q2FY27: EBITDA +27% QoQ, margin 2.9% to 3.1%. But the Q2 call still calls competition elevated. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
Margin targets keep moving. QC: 5-6% of NOV (Q3FY26), then 3-3.5% (Q4FY26). Food delivery: 5-6%, then 'flattish' for 1-2 years. [Q3FY26/Q4FY26/Q2FY27 calls]
Stores +50% times per-store NOV +16-17% implies about 75% NOV growth. That matches the 77.6% revenue growth, so the volume story checks out. [Q2FY27 call] [Numbers]
guidance: $1B adjusted EBITDA by FY29, kept 'as of now'. Asked if they are comfortable with it, management said 'no comments'. [Q4FY26 call] [Q2FY27 call]
QC: 60% order CAGR to FY29. FY27 growth below 100%, no number given. 3,000 dark stores by March 2027. [Q4FY26 call]
QC NOV growth to speed up YoY from the December quarter. Store NOV per day to reach Rs 11 lakh from Rs 9 lakh. [Q2FY27 call]
QC margin at the top of the 5-6% range. Food delivery margin flat for 1-2 years while reinvesting in growth. [Q1FY27 call] [Q2FY27 call]
Capex per store below Rs 2.5 cr. Working capital to 12 days from 14. Dark.ai capex not meaningful near term. [Q1FY27 call] [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.delivered: Dropped in Q4FY26. Q2FY27 revenue +77.6% YoY; implied NOV growth about 75%

bull: EBITDA rose six quarters in a row to Rs 752 cr. Q2 annualised is Rs 3,008 cr, 2.5x FY26's Rs 1,208 cr. [Numbers]
QC broke even in Q3FY26. Cities making up over 70% of NOV in some mature cities are EBITDA positive. QC margin guided to top of 5-6%. [Q3FY26/Q2FY27/Q1FY27 calls]
Debt is low: D/E 0.18 on Rs 31,275 cr net worth leaves room to borrow for the 60% order CAGR plan. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
bear: At 673x P/E and 0.38% ROE, the price assumes the full $1B FY29 EBITDA. Management gave 'no comments' on comfort. [Numbers] [Q2FY27 call]
FCF negative two years running, Rs -1,114 cr in FY26. Analysts noted capex grew 150% while NOV grew 60%. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
Guidance keeps slipping: 100% QC growth dropped within a quarter. CEO resigned Feb 2026. Tier-2/3 economics unproven at scale. [Q4FY26 call] [AR FY26] [Q2FY27 call]
questions: What was quick-commerce adjusted EBITDA as % of NOV in Q2FY27, by city cohort?
Why did FY26 PAT fall 31% while EBITDA rose 90%?
When does FCF turn positive, and how much debt funds the store rollout?
Food delivery margin: 5-6% steady state, or flat for two years? Which holds?

annual_report.business: Eternal operates a technology-enabled multi-segment platform in India providing food delivery, quick commerce (e-grocery), going-out experiences (dining, movies, events), and B2B restaurant supplies. Revenue from marketplace commissions, platform fees, and direct inventory-based sales.

segments.name: Quick Commerce
segments.comment: Largest segment, 626% growth YoY; shifted to inventory model for pricing control

segments.name: Food Delivery
segments.comment: Core business, 26% growth; driven by order volumes and revenue per order

segments.name: B2B Supplies
segments.comment: Declined 13%; core restaurant supplies growing despite non-restaurant business scale-down

segments.name: Going-out
segments.comment: 32% growth; first full year post-entertainment ticketing acquisition

annual_report.revenue_mix: Predominantly India-based, concentrated in top-tier urban metros. Quick commerce revenue now includes full monetary value of goods sold (not just commissions) following inventory model transition.
strategy: Shift from rapid expansion to disciplined cost efficiency and profitability focus
Inventory-owned quick commerce model for margin and pricing control
EV-based logistics transition to mitigate fuel costs and macro headwinds
Scale user retention through affordability features and consumer-centric offerings
Establish exclusive partnerships for premium event inventory access
annual_report.outlook: Management prioritizes sustained efficiency, operational discipline, and differentiated consumer offerings to maintain ecosystem leadership. Focus on long-term value creation and regulatory compliance amid intensifying competition.
annual_report.capex_plans: Strategic EV-based logistics transition mentioned for Zomato and Blinkit; specific capital expenditure amounts not disclosed in provided sections.
risks: Intensifying competition from capital-fueled quick commerce rivals with aggressive pricing tactics
Evolving regulatory framework including new Labor Codes and stringent platform governance requirements
Labor volatility and gig worker strikes threatening last-mile fulfillment continuity and order volumes
Macro-economic fluctuations and geopolitical volatility compressing consumer spending and logistics margins
annual_report.flags: CEO transition: Deepinder Goyal resigned Feb 1, 2026; Albinder Dhindsa appointed. Multiple subsidiary dissolutions in FY26. Clean unmodified audit opinions. No dividend recommended. No material contingent liabilities disclosed.
